cues: Situational irony: she dislikes the man she has never met and is drawn to the man who ignores her.
Euphemism: she calls her desire only a folly.

text: The devices to quote. Situational irony: she dislikes the man she has never met and is drawn to the man who ignores her. Free indirect style. The antithesis on the bench. Allusion to Whitman. Euphemism: she calls her desire only a folly. Foreshadowing: I should like him better if he did give me trouble. And the open ending.
